//: What is on a developer's machine after scripts/dev-aws-seed.sh.
The address is what scripts/dev-aws-seed.sh reads to know which account
to ensure exists, and it is safe to commit: .test is a reserved TLD (RFC
2606), so it can never be a real mailbox and Cognito can never mail a
stranger. seeds/staging.json cannot do the same and says why.
isAdmin and accessAllCases are both true because this is the only seat in
the firm: an admin who could not see its cases would have to add a second
person before doing anything, and a non-admin would reproduce the lockout
the seeder exists to break.
NO PASSWORD HERE, unlike seeds/staging.json, and that is the difference
between the two environments rather than an omission. A fixture person
with a password is one the loader will CREATE; without one, the account
must already exist. dev-aws-seed.sh creates it BEFORE invoking the loader
(password from ~/.config/insolvia/dev.env or a no-echo prompt — outside
the repo, because a password a human typed must never end up in a
committed fixture). The loader still resolves the address to its Cognito
sub and refuses if there is nobody to resolve.
`handle` names this person for anything that needs to refer to them; the
API's own parser ignores it.
`cases` names which cases from a committed fixture version
(seeds/fixtures/<version>/cases.json) are loaded into which firm, and
who opened them. The rows AND the sample documents converge on every
load — this machine gets the same synthetic Chapter 7 matter every other
environment gets, with the same two documents copied server-side from
the shared fixture bucket. Rows that already exist are left alone; a
changed fixture is a new version, not an edit to one that has loaded.
